title: Attorney General James and Mayor Owens sue Syracuse apartment owners over safety violations
text:
Attorney General James and Mayor Owens sue Syracuse apartment owners over safety violations
New York Attorney General Letitia James and Syracuse Mayor Sharon Owens announced on July 15 a lawsuit against the owners and managers of Nob Hill Apartments for years of persistent health and safety issues, tenants’ rights violations, and illegal business practices. The lawsuit follows 413 city and state code violations cited against Nob Hill from 2019 to 2026, with 69 still unresolved as of June. A fire in February claimed a life and displaced dozens of tenants, while another fire occurred in May; despite these incidents, unresolved fire safety violations remain.
Residents have reported pest infestations, lack of heating or air conditioning, sewage backups, broken elevators, overflowing trash, broken doors and locks leading to thefts and fights, as well as other dangerous conditions left unaddressed. The lawsuit seeks restitution for tenants—including the return of withheld security deposits—rent abatement, penalties paid to the City of Syracuse for code violations, and reimbursement for illegal fees charged to tenants such as monthly “technology” or “pest” fees that provided no clear benefit.
“The deadly fire at Nob Hill Apartments was a shameful, preventable tragedy,” said Attorney General James. “New Yorkers should never pay the price for their landlord’s negligence, and residents of Nob Hill have suffered too long in unacceptable conditions. I am grateful to Mayor Owens for her partnership in our fight to get justice for every tenant.”
Mayor Owens said, “The fire and tragic loss of life at the Nob Hill apartments is both heartbreaking and unacceptable. For decades, Nob Hill stood as a source of quality housing in our community... These owners need to be held accountable for this neglect.” Other officials including Congressman John W. Mannion said, “I applaud Attorney General James and Mayor Owens for taking action to hold Nob Hill accountable... unsafe housing... will not be tolerated.”
Attorney General James has recently filed several lawsuits addressing unsafe housing conditions across New York State. These include actions under her office’s de facto rent stabilization compliance program in June 2026; settlements with landlords over lead hazards; lawsuits targeting hazardous living conditions; actions against overcharging rent-stabilized tenants; as well as winning cases involving manufactured home parks endangering residents.
The New York Attorney General operates through regional offices across the state offering services such as consumer fraud investigations and tenant dispute mediation while promoting social justice through civil rights enforcement, according to the official website. Letitia James heads this public law enforcement agency which protects New Yorkers by upholding consumer protections among other responsibilities.
